preconditions.description: The number of people in the society is between 1 and 200, inclusive.
The number of friendships in the society is between n-1 and 2000, inclusive.
Each person is represented by a unique integer between 1 and n, inclusive.
No person is friends with themselves.
The value of b indicates the direction of envy, where 0 means the direction is unknown and 1 means the direction is known.

preconditions.expression: There is at most one friendship between each pair of people.
preconditions.description: Each pair of people has at most one friendship.

preconditions.expression: The graph represented by the friendships is connected.
preconditions.description: The graph formed by the friendships is a connected graph.

postconditions.description: The output is either 'YES' if it is possible for the society to be capitalist, or 'NO' if it is not.

postconditions.expression: output == 'YES' ==> (1 <= max_income_inequality <= 10^6 and 0 <= a_i <= 10^6 for all i)
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', then the maximum possible income inequality is between 1 and 10^6, and each person's income is between 0 and 10^6.

postconditions.expression: output == 'YES' ==> (a_i - a_j == 1 if (i, j, 1) is in the input and (j, i, 1) is not, for all i, j)
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', then for every pair of friends where the direction of envy is known, the envious person has exactly 1 more unit of income than the other.

postconditions.expression: output == 'YES' ==> (a_i - a_j <= 1 if (i, j, 0) is in the input, for all i, j)
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', then for every pair of friends where the direction of envy is unknown, the envious person has at most 1 more unit of income than the other.
If the output is 'YES', then the maximum income inequality is the difference between the maximum and minimum incomes.
